newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Bradesco Seguros buys stake in company.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Bradesco Seguros buys stake in company.

text.p: Brazil's second largest insurance group Bradesco Seguros has acquired a 40 percent stake in car insurance company Indiana Seguros for 18 million reais, an official of Indiana Seguros said.

"Bradesco Seguros has become a partner of Indiana Seguros," Claudio Afif Domingos, Indiana Seguros surperintendent, told Reuters. The remaining 60 percent stake will remain in the hands of the Afif Domingos family, he said.
The acquisition will allow Indiana Seguros to expand its insurance business and double its current premiums of 160 million reais over the next two years, he added.

Currently, Indiana Seguros has a portfolio of 120,000 auto policies while Bradesco Seguros, the insurance arm of Brazil's largest retail bank Bradesco, has 800,000 car policies in its portfolio, Domingos said.
Indiana Seguros is Brazil's 27th largest insurance company, according to the National Federation of Insurance Firms (Fenaseg).

Brazilian insurance firms have been merging with local counterparts and foreign companies to boost competitiveness and increase business in a market that is expected to grow 15 percent annually over the next decade.
